## Overview

The `cori.data.ipeds` package provides access to National Center for
Education Statistics Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System
(IPEDS) data at the county and institution levels from 2010 to the
present. IPEDS is the annual census of U.S. postsecondary institutions.
Reporting is mandatory for institutions that participate in Title IV
federal student aid programs, which is most of the universe so IPEDS is
effectively a census rather than a sample.

NCES distributes IPEDS as about a dozen separate component surveys per
year, each with its own grain and its own identifier conventions. This
package harmonizes four of its files: Institutional Characteristics,
Completions awards, Completions completers, and Graduation Rates. It
brings them into a single consistent interface and aggregates them to
counties so higher education can be analyzed alongside the rest of the
`cori.data` ecosystem.

Beyond access, the package adds the layers that make IPEDS usable
without reading NCES documentation first. Negative sentinel codes
(`-1`, `-2`, `-3`, meaning not reported, not applicable and not
available) are converted to `NA` rather than left as integers that
silently corrupt any mean. Identifiers stay character, so `unitid`
keeps its leading zeros and `cipcode` stays in the zero-padded
`"xx.xxxx"` form that joins correctly for the 01 through 09 CIP
families. County aggregations are restricted to degree-granting
institutions and exclude NCES's grand-total rows, second majors and
certificates. Every categorical column — 20 of them — carries its value
labels in the codebook, so a `sector_code` of 4 can be resolved without
leaving R.

The package also includes the NCES CIP-to-SOC crosswalk in both
vintages, which turns degree production into a measure of occupational
supply.

Variables that are rates or shares carry an `agg_var` column consistent
with the rest of the ecosystem: the adjusted cohort for graduation
rates, total degrees for degree shares, so `value * agg_var` recovers a
raw count and counties can be rolled up with correct weighting.

## Installation & quick start

```{r}
#| eval: false
remotes::install_github("ruralinnovation/cori.data.ipeds")
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(cori.data.ipeds)

# See all available variables, their coverage, and value labels
get_ipeds_codebook()

# Institutional presence and composition
get_institutions(geoids = "33009", years = 2024)

# Degrees conferred
get_degrees(geoids = "33009", years = 2024)

# Students completing — distinct from degrees
get_completers(geoids = "33009", years = 2024)

# Completion outcomes
get_graduation_rates(geoids = "33009", years = 2012:2023)

# Everything about a county, across all four functions
get_ipeds(geoids = "33009", years = 2024)
```

`geography` selects the geographic unit. County is tidy long; institution is
point-level and wide, retaining NCES's CIP detail:

```{r}
#| eval: false
get_degrees(geography = "institution", geoids = "33009", years = 2024)
```

Map programs to occupations:

```{r}
#| eval: false
get_cip_soc_crosswalk("2020")   # CIP 2020 to SOC 2018, for 2020 onward
get_cip_soc_crosswalk("2010")   # CIP 2010 to SOC 2010, for 2010-2019
```

## What this data tells us about rural America  

Rural colleges and universities are assets before they are statistics. A
college can be among the largest employers in its county, with a payroll
and a physical footprint that do not relocate, and it tends to supply the
arts, athletics and public gathering spaces a rural community might
otherwise lack. It produces the credentials that raise local educational
attainment, which means a county with an active institution has a way of
building human capital in place rather than importing it.

Presence alone is a thin reading of that asset. What an institution
grants, at what volume, and relative to the population it serves are the
questions that separate an active anchor from an address on a list. So is
what kind of institution it is. Rural higher education is roughly twice
as public as nonrural higher education, and its largest single category
is the public two-year college where the nonrural sector's is the
private four-year — structurally different sectors, with different
exposure to state appropriations and enrollment pressure.

The footprint is also wider than the county. In rural areas access often
depends on drive time, and an institution may draw students, employ staff
and place graduates across more than one county. Of the rural counties
with no four-year institution of their own, most border a county that
has one, so a measure built on presence within county lines understates
rural access considerably. The same boundary cuts the other way: a
college town's entire degree production is credited to its host county
even where that capacity serves a wider region.

## Introduction

*Adapted from the [Introduction
vignette](https://github.com/ruralinnovation/cori.data.ipeds/blob/main/vignettes/introduction.Rmd)
on GitHub.*

### What is this data?

IPEDS is the annual census NCES collects from U.S. postsecondary
institutions. Reporting is mandatory for the institutions that
participate in Title IV federal student aid programs — 5,837 of the
6,163 institutions in the 2023–24 collection — so IPEDS covers a
universe rather than a sample. The universe is shrinking: 7,503
institutions in 2010, 6,072 in 2024.

NCES distributes it as about a dozen separate survey files per year.
This package harmonizes four:

| Measure | Getter | NCES file | Grain of the source file |
|---|---|---|---|
| Institutional characteristics | `get_institutions()` | `HD{year}` | One row per institution |
| Degrees conferred | `get_degrees()` | `C{year}_A` | Institution × CIP × award level × major number |
| Students completing | `get_completers()` | `C{year}_C` | Institution × award level category |
| Graduation rates | `get_graduation_rates()` | `GR{year}` | Institution × cohort type × status |

Not covered: enrollment (`EF`), finance (`F`), staff (`S`), admissions
(`ADM`), student financial aid (`SFA`) and outcome measures (`OM`).

Data is available at the **county and institution levels** from **2010
to the present**, with two exceptions: completers begin in 2012, because
NCES published no `C_C` file before that, and graduation rates lag the
other surveys by about a year.

### Two levels: county and institution

`geography` selects the geographic unit, the same as in other cori.data
packages. IPEDS is collected from institutions rather than places, so
the finest unit available here is the institution itself — every record
carries coordinates, address, city and county — and county output
aggregates those points.

```{r}
#| eval: false
# County level (default): tidy long, one row per geoid x year x variable
get_degrees(geoids = "33009", years = 2024)

# Institution level: wide, one row per institution and the survey's own
# dimensions -- CIP code, award level, cohort type
get_degrees(geography = "institution", geoids = "33009", years = 2024)
```

The county level is an aggregation restricted to degree-granting
institutions, with NCES's grand-total rows, second majors and
certificates already excluded. The institution level is deliberately
unfiltered — it keeps everything NCES publishes, including the CIP
detail, so you can aggregate on your own terms.

Two things to know before using the output:

- **`variables` applies to the county level only.** At institution level
  the output is wide, so select columns after the call.
- **Absence is represented by no row.** A county with no degree-granting
  institution does not appear in the county output. Start joins from a
  full county list, or the counties the question is about drop out
  silently.

### What this package changes

Both levels differ from the raw NCES files in the same ways:

- **Canonical names.** `COUNTYCD` becomes `geoid`, `AWLEVEL` becomes
  `ed_level`. `get_ipeds_codebook()` is the mapping, and it drives the
  ETL rather than merely documenting it.
- **Sentinels become `NA`.** NCES codes "not reported", "not applicable"
  and "not available" as `-1`, `-2` and `-3`.
- **Identifiers stay character.** `unitid` zero-padded to six digits and
  `cipcode` to `"xx.xxxx"`, so CIP families 01 through 09 keep their
  leading zero.
- **Derived flags are added.** `is_public`, `is_4yr`,
  `is_degree_granting`, `is_hbcu`, `is_tribal` and others, computed from
  `sector_code` and the NCES status codes. These overlap rather than
  partition: all 35 tribal colleges are also land-grant institutions
  (under the 1994 designation, not the Morrill Acts), and 22 of the 102
  HBCUs are land-grant, so they cannot be cross-tabulated as mutually
  exclusive categories.

### Decoding categorical variables

The institution level returns NCES's bare integers. The codebook's
`codes` column carries the value labels for all 20 categorical columns.

```{r}
#| eval: false
cb <- get_ipeds_codebook()

# Which variables are categorical?
cb[nzchar(cb$codes), c("variable", "label")]

# What do sector_code's numbers mean?
cb$codes[cb$variable == "sector_code"]
```

### Understanding agg_var

Variables that are rates or shares include an `agg_var` column — the
weight needed to aggregate correctly across counties. An unweighted mean
gives a 40-student county the same weight as a 40,000-student one.

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(dplyr)

rates <- get_graduation_rates(geography = "county", years = 2023)

rates |>
  filter(variable == "grad_rate_150pct") |>
  summarize(
    weighted   = sum(value * agg_var, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(agg_var, na.rm = TRUE),
    unweighted = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

### Counting conventions

The institution tables are unfiltered because the right filter depends
on the question. Three NCES conventions will inflate a naive sum:

- **`cipcode == "99.0000"`** is each institution's grand total across
  programs, included alongside the per-program rows.
- **`major_num == 2`** is the second major of a double-majoring student.
- **Certificates are not degrees.** `ed_level` spans certificates
  through doctorates; the county variables count codes 3, 5, 7, 17, 18
  and 19 only.

The first two together inflate a 2024 national degree count from 4.14
million to 8.46 million. The county getters apply all three already.

Two further limits are worth stating plainly. IPEDS measures production,
not attainment — a degree is credited to the county of the institution,
not the student's home — and enrollment is absent, so any
enrollment-based measure, including online and distance education, needs
the IPEDS Enrollment (`EF`) component added first.

## Rural higher education

*Adapted from the [Rural Higher Education
vignette](https://github.com/ruralinnovation/cori.data.ipeds/blob/main/vignettes/rural-higher-education.Rmd)
on GitHub.*

This section compares rural and nonrural counties across all four
measures, using `ruraldefinitions::cbsa_2023` for the rural split, then
links degrees to the occupations they prepare students for.

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(cori.data.ipeds)
library(cori.data.pep)
library(ruraldefinitions)
library(cori.charts)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

load_fonts()

YR <- 2024

degrees    <- get_degrees(years = YR)
completers <- get_completers(years = YR)
grad_rates <- get_graduation_rates(years = 2010:2023)

rural <- cbsa_2023 |> select(geoid, is_rural)
```

### Where the four-year institutions are

Identifying counties with a four-year institution requires
institution-level data, because the county-level variables count
institutions without distinguishing which ones offer bachelor's degrees.
A county with no degree-granting institution produces no row, so the
join starts from the full county list.

```{r}
#| eval: false
has_university <- get_institutions(geography = "institution", years = YR) |>
  filter(is_degree_granting == 1, is_4yr == 1, !is.na(geoid)) |>
  distinct(geoid) |>
  mutate(has_university = TRUE)

rural |>
  left_join(has_university, by = "geoid") |>
  mutate(has_university = coalesce(has_university, FALSE)) |>
  group_by(is_rural) |>
  summarize(
    counties    = n(),
    with_uni    = sum(has_university),
    pct_without = 100 * mean(!has_university),
    .groups     = "drop"
  )
```

### Reach beyond the host county

A county without a campus may still be served by one next door. The
package is county-keyed, so build adjacency from county geometry and
check presence across each county's neighbors.

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(sf)

counties <- tigris::counties(cb = TRUE, year = 2023, progress_bar = FALSE)
neighbors <- st_touches(counties)

has_4yr <- get_institutions(geography = "institution", years = YR) |>
  filter(is_degree_granting == 1, is_4yr == 1) |>
  distinct(geoid) |>
  pull(geoid)

access <- tibble(
  geoid    = counties$GEOID,
  in_county = counties$GEOID %in% has_4yr,
  adjacent  = vapply(
    neighbors,
    function(i) any(counties$GEOID[i] %in% has_4yr),
    logical(1)
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    access = case_when(
      in_county ~ "In county",
      adjacent  ~ "Adjacent county",
      TRUE      ~ "Neither"
    )
  )

access |>
  inner_join(rural, by = "geoid") |>
  count(is_rural, access)
```

For 2024 this gives 341 rural counties with a four-year institution in
county, 1,169 adjacent to one, and 473 with neither — so a presence-only
measure treats 1,169 rural counties as lacking access to a four-year
institution when they border one.

### Composition, from the institution level

```{r}
#| eval: false
get_institutions(geography = "institution", years = YR) |>
  inner_join(rural, by = "geoid") |>
  # the level filter matters: without it, the 71 degree-granting
  # less-than-two-year institutions fall into the "Two-year" bucket
  filter(is_degree_granting == 1, is_4yr == 1 | is_2yr == 1) |>
  mutate(
    level   = if_else(is_4yr == 1, "Four-year", "Two-year"),
    control = if_else(is_public == 1, "Public", "Private")
  ) |>
  count(is_rural, level, control) |>
  group_by(is_rural) |>
  mutate(share = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup()
```

### Degrees conferred per resident

Population comes from `cori.data.pep` on the same `geoid`.

```{r}
#| eval: false
pop <- get_population(geography = "county", years = YR) |>
  filter(variable == "population") |>
  select(geoid, population = value)

rural |>
  inner_join(pop, by = "geoid") |>
  left_join(
    degrees |> filter(variable == "count_degrees_total") |>
      select(geoid, degrees = value),
    by = "geoid"
  ) |>
  mutate(degrees = coalesce(degrees, 0)) |>
  group_by(is_rural) |>
  summarize(per_1k = 1000 * sum(degrees) / sum(population), .groups = "drop")
```

### Completion rates over time

Rates cover the full-time, first-time bachelor's cohort at four-year
institutions, weighted by `agg_var` when counties are combined.

```{r}
#| eval: false
trend <- grad_rates |>
  filter(variable == "grad_rate_150pct") |>
  inner_join(rural, by = "geoid") |>
  group_by(year, is_rural) |>
  summarize(rate = sum(value * agg_var) / sum(agg_var), .groups = "drop")
```

### From degrees to occupations

SOC major group 15 is Computer and Mathematical Occupations. The
crosswalk is many-to-many, so collapse to a distinct CIP set *before*
joining — otherwise the join multiplies rows and inflates the sum.

```{r}
#| eval: false
xw <- get_cip_soc_crosswalk("2020")

cips <- xw |>
  filter(grepl("^15-", soc_code)) |>
  distinct(cip_code) |>
  pull(cip_code)

tech <- get_degrees(geography = "institution", years = 2022:2024) |>
  filter(
    cipcode %in% cips,
    major_num == 1L,              # first majors only
    cipcode != "99.0000",         # drop NCES grand-total rows
    ed_level %in% c(3L, 5L, 7L, 17L, 18L, 19L)
  ) |>
  group_by(geoid) |>
  summarize(tech_degrees = sum(count_total_students), .groups = "drop")

rural |>
  left_join(tech, by = "geoid") |>
  mutate(tech_degrees = coalesce(tech_degrees, 0)) |>
  group_by(is_rural) |>
  summarize(degrees = sum(tech_degrees), .groups = "drop")
```

Match the crosswalk vintage to the completions year: `"2010"` for
2010–2019 and `"2020"` for 2020 onward, when NCES moved to the CIP 2020
taxonomy. Pairing a year with the wrong vintage usually runs without
error, which is why it's worth setting deliberately.

### Filtering to one state

```{r}
#| eval: false
# This lists only counties that contain an institution; start from a full
# county list before joining other data.
state_counties <- get_institutions(geography = "institution", years = YR) |>
  filter(st_abbr == "MT") |>
  distinct(geoid) |>
  pull(geoid)

get_degrees(geoids = state_counties, years = YR)
get_graduation_rates(geoids = state_counties, years = 2010:2023)
```
